base: vintage 19th-century storybook pen-and-ink engraving, black and white line art, fine cross-hatching and stippling, etching illustration, clean off-white background, light airy line art, mostly white, pure line art (NOT watercolor, no grey wash, NOT dark). WIDE HORIZONTAL LANDSCAPE orientation, 3:2 aspect ratio, much wider than tall. RECURRING CHARACTER A, THE YOUNG WOODCUTTER (must look identical in every image): a tall athletic MAN of about 25, broad shoulders, thick forearms, clean-shaven, short dark hair, NO hat, plain 19th-century rural work clothes - collarless linen shirt with sleeves rolled above the elbow, suspenders, worn trousers, leather boots, a long-handled felling axe. RECURRING CHARACTER B, THE OLD WOODCUTTER (must look identical in every image): a lean wiry MAN of about 70, short white beard, deeply lined weathered face, calm eyes, a soft cloth flat cap, a wool waistcoat over a collarless shirt, worn trousers, leather boots, a pipe, a short-handled axe. Both are working men, NOT gentlemen: no top hat, no frock coat, no tie. Realistic proportions between the two men. RECURRING SETTING: the edge of an old pine and oak forest, a small log cabin with a stone chimney, fresh-cut stumps and felled logs on the ground, and a hand-cranked round GRINDSTONE wheel on a wooden stand beside the cabin. No other people, no crowd. Whimsical, elegant, highly detailed, classic fairytale book plate. COMPOSITION: keep every person and the main subject inside the CENTRAL two thirds of the frame, with empty margin on the left and right edges; nothing important near the side edges. NO text, NO words, NO letters, NO signage, NO numbers, NO logos, NO lettering anywhere, no color.

images.scene: SCENE: dawn at the forest edge. The young woodcutter and the old woodcutter stand FACING EACH OTHER in profile, a few steps apart, each with his axe resting on his shoulder, about to start a wager. The young man stands tall, chest out, confident and imposing; the old man stands relaxed and calm, pipe in his mouth, a faint knowing smile. Rows of tall pines behind them, the log cabin small at one side, low morning light. Medium shot, both men full-length. NO grindstone wheel anywhere in the picture.

SCENE: HIGH WIDE ESTABLISHING SHOT from an elevated viewpoint, looking down at a slant over a large clearing at the forest edge. In the middle of the clearing the two woodcutters, small in the frame, are SHAKING HANDS to seal the wager, their axes leaning against a stump beside them. The log cabin stands near them; long rows of tall standing pines wait on both sides of the clearing. Early morning, long soft shadows, mostly white sky. NO grindstone wheel anywhere in the picture.

SCENE: CLOSE-UP PORTRAIT, head and shoulders, of the YOUNG woodcutter only. His face is turned to face the RIGHT edge of the frame in three-quarter profile, chin raised, jaw set, confident and eager, the long axe handle resting on his shoulder, sleeves rolled, thick forearm visible. Pine trunks softly behind. Only ONE man in the picture.

SCENE: CLOSE-UP PORTRAIT, head and shoulders, of the OLD woodcutter only. His face is turned to face the LEFT edge of the frame in three-quarter profile, short white beard, lined weathered face, cloth flat cap, pipe in the corner of his mouth, a calm knowing half-smile, the short axe resting on his shoulder. Pine trunks softly behind. Only ONE man in the picture.

SCENE: DRAMATIC LOW-ANGLE HERO SHOT from ground level looking UP. The young woodcutter, alone, in the middle of a powerful axe swing, body twisted, muscles tense, wood chips flying from the deep notch in a tall pine trunk that is beginning to tilt and fall. Sky mostly white above him, tall trunks converging upward. Raw strength and speed. Only the young man in the picture.

SCENE: seen from BEHIND, at ground level. COMPOSITION IS CRITICAL: both men must sit INSIDE the central 60% of the frame width, with wide empty margins of clearing on the far left and far right edges; nothing important touches the side edges. In the near foreground, LARGE, standing at about one third from the left edge and fully inside the frame including his whole axe, the YOUNG woodcutter is mid-swing chopping a tall pine, back to the camera, chips flying, sweat on his shirt. FAR AWAY at about two thirds from the left edge, SMALL but clearly visible (about the height of the young man's boot), at the far edge of the clearing near the tree line, the OLD woodcutter sits on a stump with his BACK to the camera, cap and a thread of pipe smoke, so far off that nobody could tell what he is doing. A long empty stretch of clearing with stumps and felled logs separates the two men, showing how much distance has opened between them. Wide open space, mostly white sky. Only these two men.

SCENE: CLOSE-UP of the YOUNG woodcutter's face and shoulders as he looks back OVER HIS SHOULDER toward the cabin, grinning with a cocky half-smile, sweat on his brow, hair damp, axe handle gripped in one hand. Behind him a fresh-cut stump and pine trunks. Only the young man in the picture, cabin tiny and far in the background.

SCENE: a FOUR-PANEL comic-strip page, 2 by 2 grid of four EQUAL square panels separated by thin white gutters, each panel a complete engraved scene showing time passing across one day. Panel 1 (top left): morning sun low, the OLD woodcutter ALONE sitting on a stump with his BACK to the viewer, axe across his lap, pipe smoke rising, apparently resting; nobody else in this panel. Panel 2 (top right): sun higher, the OLD woodcutter ALONE chopping a tree, calm and steady; nobody else in this panel. Panel 3 (bottom left): afternoon sun, the OLD woodcutter ALONE walking slowly away from the trees with his axe on his shoulder, going to sit down again; nobody else in this panel. Panel 4 (bottom right): low evening sun, the YOUNG woodcutter ALONE still chopping furiously, sweat flying, surrounded by many stumps. Same two men and same clothes in every panel. The young woodcutter appears ONLY in panel 4; panels 1, 2 and 3 show only the old man. Nothing in any panel shows what the old man does while resting. NO captions, NO speech bubbles, NO panel numbers.

SCENE: TOP-DOWN ZENITAL VIEW looking STRAIGHT DOWN from directly overhead, camera pointing vertically at the ground, bird's eye. NO horizon and NO sky anywhere, only the ground seen from above. Two separate stacks of felled tree trunks lie side by side on the clearing floor, seen from straight above as rows of round log ends: the stack on the LEFT is clearly SMALLER, the stack on the RIGHT is clearly BIGGER, about twice as many logs. At the bottom edge of the frame the two woodcutters stand side by side seen from straight above, only the tops of their heads and shoulders, tiny, looking at the stacks. Stumps and sawdust around. Dusk, long shadows.

SCENE: medium shot at eye level. The YOUNG woodcutter stands with his axe DROPPED on the ground at his feet, both hands open and raised in a baffled questioning gesture, brow furrowed, exhausted and confused, shirt soaked. Facing him, the OLD woodcutter sits calmly on a stump, pipe in his mouth, his short axe across his knees, looking up at him with patient eyes. Dusk light, the cabin behind. NO grindstone wheel anywhere in the picture.

SCENE: INTIMATE EXTREME CLOSE-UP. Only the OLD woodcutter's weathered hands, sleeves rolled, seated on a stump with the short axe laid across his knee: one hand steadies the axe head, the other hand holds a small hand-held WHETSTONE (a flat oval sharpening stone that fits in the palm, the kind a woodsman carries in his pocket) and draws it along the axe blade edge in a slow stroke; a faint bright line on the steel where the stone has passed, a little stone dust. His waistcoat and trouser knee visible, face out of frame. Shallow depth, forest floor and stumps soft behind. Fine detail on the hands, the stone and the steel edge. NO grindstone wheel.

SCENE: MACRO STILL LIFE, no people. Two REAL, ANATOMICALLY CORRECT felling axes lie side by side on top of the same broad fresh-cut stump, in one continuous scene, both seen from the same angle with the cutting edge toward the camera. Each axe is a classic woodsman's felling axe: a heavy SOLID forged-steel head shaped like a wedge, with a flat POLL at the back, an EYE through which the long curved hickory handle passes, and a narrow curved CUTTING BIT along the front edge only - the bit is a thin bevelled strip about a finger wide at the very front of the head; the rest of the head is thick plain steel, NOT a blade. The LEFT axe's bit is DULL: the edge is rounded, nicked and rolled over, with small chips missing and dark rust along the bevel. The RIGHT axe's bit is FRESHLY SHARPENED: a clean bright bevel line runs only along the narrow front edge, catching the light, the rest of the head dark and plain. Wood chips and sawdust on the stump, forest floor soft behind. No hands, no people. Realistic tool anatomy like a 19th-century hardware catalogue engraving.

SCENE: slightly elevated three-quarter shot, late afternoon. The YOUNG woodcutter sits alone on a stump, shoulders slumped, exhausted, his long axe lying ACROSS HIS KNEES, head bowed as he stares at the dull blade in his hands, turning it over. Many stumps around him, the forest edge behind, light sky. Quiet, reflective mood, mostly white background. NO grindstone wheel anywhere in the picture.

SCENE: OVER-THE-SHOULDER POINT OF VIEW from just behind the YOUNG woodcutter's shoulder, looking down. The young man sits on a stump with his long axe across his knees, his big hands holding a small hand-held WHETSTONE (a flat oval sharpening stone that fits in the palm, the kind a woodsman carries in his pocket) against the blade; the OLD woodcutter crouches beside him, his weathered hands gently guiding the angle of the young man's wrist and the stone, teaching him the stroke. Both faces in three-quarter profile, focused, the old man patient with his pipe, the young man attentive. Stumps and the forest edge behind, the cabin small and far. NO grindstone wheel.

SCENE: DRAMATIC LOW-ANGLE HERO SHOT from ground level looking UP, the next morning. The YOUNG woodcutter, alone, completes ONE clean powerful swing, his freshly sharpened axe blade gleaming with a bright edge, and a tall pine comes down in one piece, a clean smooth cut in the trunk, few chips. He looks steady and composed, not frantic. Bright morning sky, mostly white. Only the young man in the picture.

SCENE: seen from BEHIND at dawn. The YOUNG woodcutter stands still at the forest edge, back to the camera, his sharpened axe resting on his shoulder with the blade catching the light, looking out at a long row of tall standing pines ahead of him waiting to be cut. At one side, the log cabin; the OLD woodcutter is NOT in the picture. Long soft morning shadows, mostly white sky. Calm, ready, determined. NO grindstone wheel anywhere in the picture.
